title: Two Satellites Crashed at 26,000 MPH and Made 2,300 Pieces of Junk

scenes.text: Two satellites smashed into each other at twenty-six thousand miles an hour.
It happened on February tenth, 2009, about four hundred ninety miles above Siberia.
One was a working American communications satellite. The other was a dead Russian one.
Both were torn apart into more than two thousand trackable pieces.
Hundreds of those pieces are still orbiting Earth today.
Two satellites. One crash. Still up there.

description:
In February 2009, two satellites collided about 490 miles above Siberia at roughly 26,000 miles an hour.
It created more than 2,000 trackable pieces of debris, and hundreds are still in orbit.
Should space have traffic rules?
first_comment: Bonus: the crash happened in a busy orbit, and tracking has since found about 2,300 pieces. Do you think we should clean up space?
